summary: Check Sonnet's 121 pause-game positions against Codex's ledgers, and review the converter, before the kx3 runs use them

review.summary:
The Oct 6 batch has 66 of the 121 positions (12 games). I compared 9 positions with the ledger field by field and ran read-only scripts over all 66. The scripts checked each Pokémon's printing against the ledger's text and HP, the hand cards, each deck file against the QR printings, the Energy fields, and the effects listed on the board.

The main problem is the converter's choice of his card printings. It picks them by name only: the database's first printing, and one printing per name. It ignores the QR printing lists and the attack and ability text in the ledger, and honours only a "SET NNN" label at the start of the ledger's text. As a result, 9 of the 12 deck files are wrong. About 36 of the 66 positions have at least one wrong card of his on the board, in his hand, under an evolved card or in the discard.

Worst case: game 213625 (6 positions) has the old A1 Caterpie line instead of the B3b one. His Sunny Wind attacks become an "Attack:Gust" he cannot pay for, so km3's moves in that game are likely caused by the wrong card. In the three switch-2 games, the converted positions do not contain the switch-2 card (Togekiss A4 080, Meowth B2 124, Conkeldurr A3 096 Guts). So 16 of the batch's 21 flagged positions hold no card the switch changed; only 183108 (5 positions) really carries one.

Other problems:
- Game 020518's Energy was read as Water instead of Fighting.
- Effects on the opponent's Pokémon that change damage (Brass Rock -20, Garchomp's Mach Stealth) are dropped.
- His recorded plan never names where Wally or Turbo Shark put their extra Energy, so those turns can never count as the same plan as km3's.
- One knockout puts the wrong Pokémon's Energy into the discard.

Two positions matched the ledger in every field: 123812 t03 and 183108 t09. Points, turn count, opponent hand size, Stadium and its owner matched in all 9 compared positions.

findings.title: 213625: the whole Caterpie line is the wrong card (A1 instead of B3b), so his recorded attacks are illegal
findings.detail:
The deck file KW261004_213625000.txt has 2 Caterpie A1 005, 2 Metapod A1 006 and 2 Butterfree A1 007. The real cards are the B3b printings. Card text from card.py:
- Caterpie: A1 005 is HP 50 with Find a Friend; B3b 001 is HP 40 with the Quick Growth auto-evolve ability and [G] Hook 10.
- Metapod: A1 006 has [CC] Bug Bite 30; B3b 002 has [G] Ram 30.
- Butterfree: A1 007 is HP 120 with the Powder Heal ability and [GCC] Gust 60; B3b 003 is HP 130 with [G] Sunny Wind 60, heal 20.

What this does to each position:
- t07: his Active Butterfree is A1 007 with hp 130, above its 120 maximum, and 1 Grass. His plan ends 'Attack:Gust' (the converter's fallback to the last printed attack), which is not legal because he attaches to Accelgor.
- t09: same problem; Gust is not legal with 1 Grass on Butterfree.
- t03: his Ram KO of Budew needs [G], but the position's Metapod has Bug Bite [CC] with 1 Energy, so the KO is impossible.
- t01 to t07: Caterpie at 40 HP looks damaged on a 50-HP card.

Could change the bot's move: yes. km3's 12/12 Retreat at t07 and its Ability (Powder Heal) at t05 and t09 are likely caused by the wrong card.

findings.title: 034953: Aegislash set to Superb Shield although the ledger shows Cursed Metal at work
findings.detail:
In this game Codex's set labels contradict the attack text. The Cursed Metal card is labelled 'B2 120; Cursed Metal / Slicing Blade 70', and the other one 'B1 172; Superb Shield 80'. The Doublades have the same problem: 'B1 171; Dual Blades40x' and 'B2 119; Slash40'.

The Magnemite fix trusts the label, so every Aegislash became B2 120 (Superb Shield [MMM] 80, no ability). MAGNEMITE_CHECK's 'B1 172 → B2 120' correction is therefore wrong. The ledger records Cursed Metal adding 30 damage from T12 on, so:
- The board Aegislash at t14 and t16 should be B1 172.
- The Cursed Metal Aegislash in hand at t02-t12 should be B1 172.
- The hand Honedge at t14 and the bench Honedge at t16 ('B2 118; Cut Up20, HP70') are shown as B1 170 (HP 60; at t16 its hp 70 is above that maximum).
- The deck file has 2 Honedge B1 170, 2 Doublade B1 171 and 2 Aegislash B2 120; the QR has one of each printing for all three.

Could change the bot's move: the damage view, yes (Metal Arms does 150 instead of 180). The first moves probably not, because the KOs at t12, t14 and t16 (Haxorus 50, Happiny 30, Haxorus 150) still happen.

verdict.reasoning:
I checked this again from the source files, reading only JSON, MD and PY, and looked up card text with lib/card.py in WSL. The core of the finding holds. Three details are off: the t03 description, t05 left out of the illegal-attack list, and t11 counted as affected.

Checks that confirm it:
- Cards are B3b. QR_DECODE_RECEIPT.json (and DECK_USED.json filmed_qr_counts) gives the aliases for entity 19040 as B3b 001/091, 19050 as B3b 002/092 and 19060 as B3b 003/093.
- The ledger agrees. TURN_LEDGER.json describes his Caterpie as 'Quick Growth / Hook 10' 40/40 from T1 on, Metapod as 'Ram 30' and Butterfree as 'Sunny Wind 60' 130/130. T3 play 4 is 'Metapod ... Ram30 KO'. T5 play 4 and T7 play 3 are Sunny Wind 60, the T7 one a KO. T9 play 4 is 'Sunny Wind60'. The T8 automatic events include 'Quick Growth automatically evolves promoted Caterpie into Metapod'.
- Card text from card.py matches what the reviewer quoted:
  - Caterpie A1 005: HP 50, [C] Find a Friend. B3b 001: HP 40, Quick Growth, [G] Hook 10.
  - Metapod A1 006: [CC] Bug Bite 30. B3b 002: [G] Ram 30.
  - Butterfree A1 007: HP 120, Powder Heal, [GCC] Gust 60. B3b 003: HP 130, [G] Sunny Wind 60 with heal 20.
- The deck file KW261004_213625000.txt lists A1 005/006/007, and every position uses the A1 printings.
- Root cause in harness/ledger_to_positions.py:
  - load_deck reads filmed_qr_cards_20, whose entries have no 'variant' field. The key filmed_qr_counts, which holds printing_aliases, is never picked up.
  - So printing_for() falls back to the database's first printing, A1.
  - The ledger override (line 307) only fires on a 'SET NNN' string, and this ledger's variants are attack names.
  - Line 391 uses MINE for his own cards whatever the HP, so the note 'printings chosen by the HP shown' is not true for his side.

Effect, position by position (positions_all.json):
- t01: Active Caterpie A1 005 at hp 40, which reads as 10 damage on a 50-HP card. In the game it was 40/40 with no damage. km3 plays Lucky Ice Pop first in 4 of 12 seeds (km3_TABLES.md). Lucky Ice Pop heals the Active, so it only does something because of that phantom damage. Quick Growth is also missing.
- t03: the reviewer's wording is not exact. The position has no Metapod at the start. The Active is Caterpie A1 005 at hp 30, and the plan's last step is 'Attack:Find a Friend', the A1 Caterpie fallback the note mentions. The reason: Quick-Grow Extract goes through line 524 as a plain 'Play:' step, and the attacker's name is not updated (unlike Evolve at lines 523 and 538). The conclusion still holds: Quick-Grow Extract would fetch Metapod A1 006, whose [CC] Bug Bite cannot be paid with 1 Grass, so the Ram KO can't be reproduced. A second, separate error: with the B3b printing the converter would still write 'Attack:Hook', not Ram.
- t05: the finding names this position but leaves it out of the illegal-attack list. The plan is Poké Ball, Evolve:Butterfree@0, Attach@1 (to Shelmet), 'Attack:Gust'. Butterfree has 1 Grass and A1 Gust needs GCC, so the attack is illegal. km3's 12/12 plan includes Ability; the only Ability among his cards is A1 Powder Heal.
- t07: confirmed as stated. Butterfree A1 007 at hp 130, above its 120 maximum, with 1 Grass. The plan attaches to Accelgor@1 and then 'Attack:Gust', which is illegal. km3: Retreat:1 12/12, then Accelgor's Deck and Cover.
- t09: confirmed as stated. Evolve Butterfree@0 and Attach@0 give 1 Grass, so 'Attack:Gust' is illegal. km3 12/12: Ability (Powder Heal), then Retreat:1, then no attack.
- t11: not materially affected. No Caterpie line is on the board, in the hand or left in the deck. The 6 A1 cards sit only in the discard, and nothing in this deck uses the discard. His plan ends with Accelgor's Deck and Cover, which the printing doesn't touch.

Separate errors in the same game (I verified both, but they are not part of this finding):

All three are Kingdra ex / Team Rocket's Weezing ex, and together they gave 13 positions: 003458 t01 t03 t05 t07 t09 t11, 004128 t02 t04, and 004435 t02 t04 t06 t08 t10. None is flagged for rules switch 2. I grepped the cards seen in these games (both sides) against rl/engine-2026-10-12/*.md and the list in harness/position_list.py and found no hit, so the "two flagged positions" requirement does not apply here. I checked all 13 positions instead of 8. Most fields match the ledgers exactly: hands (card names and order), both boards (card names, HP left, attached Energy by type, Tools, order), points, opponent hand counts, Stadium and its owner, energy_next on both sides, turn count and his discard from his own plays and knockouts. findings.detail: The position's his_plan is 'Place:Horsea > Evolve:Team Rocket's Weezing ex@0 > Attach:1Water@1 zone > Play:Hiking Trail', with no Ability step. He did use Boiler Smog right after evolving: the opponent's Mega Gyarados ex ends the turn Poisoned and Burned, and checkup takes it from 210 to 180. The ledger records the Ability inside the evolution play's nested_events_in_order rather than as its own play, and the converter's plan loop (ledger_to_positions.py lines 483-581) never reads nested_events_in_order. Compare 003458 turn 7, where the same Ability is its own play (order 3, kind 'ability') and does show up in that plan as 'Ability:...@2'. This does not change what a bot does at the position. It does make the comparison wrong: km3's most common plan here includes '> Ability >' right after the Weezing ex evolution, so position_list.tsv's 'same plan 0/12' and any reading that km3 uses Boiler Smog and he does not are both partly false. Every ledger that nests an Ability triggered by evolution will lose that step the same way.

findings.title: 004435 t10: the discard is missing 3 milled cards, his Kingdra ex is Poisoned at 10 HP (not represented), and there is no plan
findings.detail: (a) On opponent turn 9, Mega Blaster discarded the top 3 cards of his deck. The ledger names the top one (Soothing Shore); the other two are unknown. The position's me.discard is only ['Poké Ball A2b 111', 'Copycat B1 225'], so Soothing Shore and two other cards are still in his deck. The converter only follows his own plays and knockouts and never reads the opponent's effects on his deck (lines 341-377). (b) His Active Kingdra ex has 10 HP left and is Poisoned. Poison does 10 at every Checkup, and retreating removes Special Conditions (RULES_FOR_AGENTS.md lines 91 and 102). So if Kingdra ex is still Active when his turn ends, it is knocked out and the opponent scores 2 points. The best line (retreat it, or knock out the 30-HP Mega Gyarados ex and accept losing Kingdra ex) depends on this, and a bot that cannot see the Poison will judge the position wrongly. This is the known status-condition limit, but this position is badly affected. (c) He played nothing: the opponent conceded and his only play was looking at Professor's Research. So no plan of his exists to compare with. Recommend leaving this position out of the expensive bot runs.

Cause: I imported ledger_to_positions.py read-only (python3 -B, no bytecode written) and called opp_card('Dragonair', 80, ledger text). It returns 'Dragonair B2b 052'.

Cited example: PAUSE_GAMES_NEW_READ_sonnet.md line 68 does cite 003458 turn 5 (km3 retreats Seadra into Horsea before Poké Ball, 12/12). The finding does not claim the printing caused that, and I did not test whether it did.

- The lost Ability does not matter in this position. At t05 the Active is Pichu, which is not a Dragon Pokémon, and the harness sets the opponent's discard Energy to []. So the real Dragon's Blessing would have nothing to do here either.

The real card could hit for 40; B2b 052 instead pulls two more zone Energy and does no damage. The retreat cost also differs (1 vs 2).

(1) The same tie-break failure is not hypothetical "in other batches". It already gives wrong printings in this 121-position set. I scanned every opponent instance at every converted owner turn with the converter's own functions, and checked the card text with lib/card.py. The failure happens whenever the ledger text does not begin with the attack title: a type word, an HP figure or an Ability name first.

KW-261010_013009000-t05/t07/t09/t11/t13/t15: 6 positions. Likely wrong, because the attack name in the ledger matches no printing exactly.

With Dragonair, that is 19 positions across 5 games from this one cause. I did not check whether other reviewers reported these.

(2) The stack under Dragonair at t05 is also wrong. The position has behind ['Dratini A1 183'] (HP 70, [WL] Ram 40). review.summary:
I found real conversion errors, so the positions are not ready for the expensive bot runs. Two problems are blockers.

(1) In 11 of the 23 games (66 of the 121 positions), some of Dustin's own cards are the wrong card. The converter keeps only one printing per card name. So when a deck holds two different cards with the same name (one Guts Conkeldurr and one Bedrock Breaker Conkeldurr, two different Aegislash, Honedge, Doublade or Meowth), both copies become the same card. Where the list gives no printing, it takes the first one in the database, and it never reads the printings that DECK_USED.json itself lists for each card. This puts the wrong cards in the deck files, hands and boards, and gives 8 positions the wrong attack in his plan.

(2) Game 20261006_020518 is a Fighting deck, but its deck file says "Energy: Water". DECK_USED stores the Energy as a list of entries the parser does not read, so it fell back to Water. Five of its 8 positions also have Water as his next Energy.

Major problems:
- 19 positions give the opponent a printing that the ledger's own text rules out: Oricorio, Revavroom (Metal Transport ability), Feebas, Charmeleon and Dragonair. The tie-break only works when the ledger's description starts with the attack name.
- Effects from the opponent's last turn are always dropped (turn_effects is always empty). Examples are Brass Rock, Mach Stealth (no damage can be done to Garchomp that turn) and Pile-Driving Hammer: 8 positions.
- His plan steps are wrong in 4 positions. A cancelled Wally is recorded as played and is his first move. In 3 positions the Boiler Smog ability is missing because the ledger logged it as a prompt answer.

Minor problems:
- In 3 turns he simply ended the turn. These came out as empty plans and were counted as "the game ended first".
- All 4 cut-short plans had readable targets. The converter could not follow them, so these are not ledger gaps.
- In one game a Caterpie that evolved during the opponent's turn was counted as knocked out.
- Some evolution stacks are wrong: a Stage 1 that Rare Candy skipped is placed under the Stage 2 in 4 positions, and the two Kingdra ex stacks are swapped in 5 positions, although the ledger's instance ids show which is which.
- The 20261010_014541 deck list is known to be the wrong version (DECK_USED says Elegant Cape was drawn and played but is missing from the list). It was used for 4 positions, and the read does not mention it.
- One position (20261006_020518 turn 13) was dropped because of a converter crash, not a ledger gap.

These parts check out: Energy by type, Tools, bench order, HP against damage, the opponent's next Energy (matches the following turn in all 111 checkable positions), hands taken after the draw, opponent hand counts, retreat payments, and the plan targets the converter did resolve.

findings.title: Dustin's own cards: one printing per name, first database printing, DECK_USED printings ignored
findings.positions: systematic: 66 positions in 11 games (60 with an affected card in hand or on the board)
findings.detail:
There are three causes in ledger_to_positions.py:

(a) Lines 295-299 keep one printing per card name (MINE.setdefault) and add the counts together. Several decks hold two different cards under one name, so one copy becomes the wrong card: 031138 Spritzee/Aromatisse/Togepi; 032023, 032857 and 033529 Aegislash; 034953 Honedge, Doublade and Aegislash; 012927 Meowth; 020518 Conkeldurr and Sandslash; 012303 and 013009 Conkeldurr.

(b) _card_entries (line 229) reads only 'variant', and load_deck prefers lists with no printings, such as cards_in_log_order or filmed_qr_cards_20. Missing printings then become the first database printing (printing_for, line 273). Meanwhile DECK_USED names the right one in printing_aliases (213625 filmed_qr_counts; 031138 counts_by_name_and_variant; 032857, 034953, 020518).

(c) The override at lines 301-314 trusts the set id Codex writes in the variant and never checks it against the attack text. In 034953 Codex swapped the ids: 'B2 120; Cursed Metal / Slicing Blade' is B1 172 in the database. So the 'correction' in MAGNEMITE_CHECK put the Superb Shield Aegislash on the board where Cursed Metal is in play.

Hand variants are ignored too. 034953 holds one of each Aegislash, but the position shows two 'Aegislash B2 120'.

Impact: the deck files hold the wrong cards, as do hands and boards. HP readings get attached to the wrong card (Meowth A1 196 shown at 50/60 HP, Honedge B1 170 at 70 with a printed 60, Butterfree A1 007 at 130 with a printed 120). Eight plan attacks are mislabelled because the attack-title fallback (line 579) silently picks the wrong card's last attack. The rules switch 2 flags for 013009 (Conkeldurr Guts), 012927 (Meowth) and 031138 (Togekiss) describe cards the positions do not hold: the deck files have 2 Conkeldurr B4 089, 2 Meowth A1 196 and 2 Togekiss A2 065.

TURN_LEDGER t05 plays_in_order attack reads 'Sunny Wind60'. KW-261004_213625000-t05, t07 and t09 his_plan have 'Attack:Gust'; t01 board Caterpie A1 005 has hp 40 (ledger variant 'Quick Growth / Hook 10', hp_max 40).

- Pile-Driving Hammer: Garganacl's attacks and retreat cost 2 more Colorless.
